purpose: Review the fish-related evidence in Vedra et al.'s 2024 aquatic-fauna paper for selected Claver river systems, documenting its useful river/estuary scope while withholding taxon-site and current-presence claims that the source does not resolve.

studySource.title: Assemblages of Aquatic Fauna in the River Systems of Claver, Surigao del Norte, Philippines
studySource.studyAreaAsTitledAndAbstracted: Selected river systems in Claver, Surigao del Norte, Philippines.

accessAndReuse.visualReview: Publisher-hosted full-text PDF text, methods, Tables 1-4 and Figure 4 captions were reviewed. No station coordinates were transcribed or digitized from Figure 1.
accessAndReuse.licenseAssessment: No article-specific Creative Commons license or Bangwit republication permission was identified in the reviewed paper or landing page. Public access is not treated as reuse permission.
accessAndReuse.decision: Keep bibliographic metadata and this concise attributed evidence-quality summary only. Do not copy the table or fish photographs into the app without an item-specific rights review.

methodsAndPlace.design: Opportunistic aquatic-fauna survey using visual encounters and reported field collections across 12 stations; the methods describe kick-net collection for aquatic fauna, while the fish-results section says locals captured fish specimens and provided local names. The fish-specific collection protocol and effort are not unambiguously separated from macroinvertebrate sampling.
methodsAndPlace.administrativePlaceConflict: The title, abstract, Figure 1 caption, Figure 4 caption and acknowledgement identify Claver, Surigao del Norte; Table 1, Table 3 and Table 4 captions instead say river systems of Surigao del Sur. The conflict is unresolved in the article; the study should not be silently reassigned or mapped pending clarification.
methodsAndPlace.freshwaterAndTidalContext: The authors describe outflow stations 4, 8 and 10 as sites of freshwater/seawater interaction, and describe tidal differences at the Hayanggabon River mouth. No salinity or station-level habitat measurement is provided to classify individual fish records.
methodsAndPlace.effortAndCount: Twelve stations were listed and three replicate samples are described, but it is unclear whether those replicates and the kick-net protocol apply to fish. The paper describes fish records as few and presents no per-taxon catch abundance in Table 4.

fishEvidence.sourceNameCaveat: Preserve names exactly as printed, including the candidate spelling Terapon jarboa and family-level Cyprinidae sp.; this review does not normalize or identify the photographed specimens.
fishEvidence.stationCrosswalk: Table 4 contains date, family, scientific name, common name and local name, but no station, river or waterbody column. Prose gives incomplete and ambiguous station groupings for three 2023 records and broad habitat descriptions for other 2022 fish; these do not establish a complete taxon-to-waterbody crosswalk.
fishEvidence.voucherStatus: Figure 4 shows fish photographs with rulers, but no voucher accessions, repository, diagnostic character measurements, specimen labels or photo-to-station/taxon chain of custody are documented.
fishEvidence.diet: No gut-content, prey-composition or diet method is reported. Commercial value and common/local names are not natural-diet evidence or bait recommendations.

evidenceDecision.localityEvidence: Historical reports of fish collected or observed at selected river-system stations during 2022-2023, with a title/abstract locality and contradictory table captions.
evidenceDecision.taxonEvidence: Eleven source labels, four of which are family/genus-level. Source label identity remains unverified; seven binomials require a separate nomenclature screen.
evidenceDecision.waterbodyEvidence: Twelve station waterbody names are printed, but no station-level fish crosswalk is provided. No exact coordinates or geometry are admitted.
evidenceDecision.waterQualityEvidence: Habitat/substrate notes and historical flow-rate estimates only; no salinity, chemical-quality or current safety measurements are accepted.
evidenceDecision.legalOrCatchabilityEvidence: None. Commercial value statements do not establish legal fishing access, local rules or present catchability.
evidenceDecision.rights: Article-specific license and Bangwit republication permission were not verified.

limitations: The title/abstract identifies Claver, Surigao del Norte, while three table captions state Surigao del Sur; no correction or erratum was located during this review.
Fish Table 4 does not map individual labels to stations, named rivers or tidal zones.

Field-method text does not clearly distinguish fish-specific capture, survey effort and kick-net replicates from macroinvertebrate sampling; the authors also attribute fish specimens to local capture.
Four labels stop at family or genus, and no taxonomic cross-check has yet been completed for the seven binomials.
No specimen accession or photo-to-site chain of custody was located; photographs alone do not verify the listed names.
Historic flow/habitat observations are not current water-quality or safety evidence; no salinity is reported for tidal sites.
No natural-diet data, current fishing law, catchability, precise geometry or item-specific reuse permission is established.
nextAction: Keep the paper as a research-only Caraga river/estuary lead. Next cross-check the seven binomials against an authoritative fish taxonomy source while preserving all labels; use the Claver-versus-Surigao-del-Sur caption conflict and missing station crosswalk to prevent public locality claims.

references.supports: Publisher landing page, bibliographic identity, abstract scope and listed Claver locality.
Publisher-hosted primary article: survey period, methods, station/waterbody table, tidal context, fish labels, photo captions and conflicting Surigao del Sur table captions.
